pageNodes.subtitle: Content the automated tests navigate to. Replaced whenever the service starts, so edits here are lost.

versions.content:
This page belongs to the automated browser tests. It is seeded under the development testing root so it never sits alongside content an editor is working on, and it is re-imported every time the seed runs, so editing it here is pointless — the next seed puts it back.

Why a wiki-typed fixture?

Most CMS pages are content-typed and rendered through Content.cshtml. Wiki pages take a separate code path (Wiki.cshtml, IHtmlRenderingService), and without a live wiki page nothing exercises it — regressions there wouldn't surface until someone manually created one.

Layout

Wiki pages use a 1/3–2/3 grid with a sibling-nav in the left column and the article body in the right.

  • Left column: sibling navigation
  • Right column: heading, subtitle, body HTML

Enough words for a good scroll

The body deliberately runs long enough that a typical laptop viewport can scroll comfortably. The back-to-top tests assert on how far the reader has travelled before the link appears, so shortening this page would quietly make those assertions vacuous.

Paragraph two — filler so the page has scroll depth for exercising the back-to-top link and any future long-form nav behaviour.

Paragraph three — additional filler so the section headings are far enough apart that the sibling nav in the sidebar has room to render the whole tree without collapsing.

Paragraph four — the final paragraph before the closing heading. When you click the back-to-top link from anywhere on the page, the browser should jump straight back to the H1 at the top of this article.

End

You have reached the end. Try the back-to-top link.

Short fixture page A deliberately short fixture. There is not enough content here to scroll, so no back-to-top link should appear.

Search fixture page This fixture exists so a site search can be relied on to return at least one hit. It carries the keyword testfixture, which nothing else in the corpus uses, so a search for that term matches this page and nothing an editor wrote. The admin search-analytics screens record a visitor's search and then show the hits it produced. Those tests used to search for a word that merely happened to be somewhere in the content, which made them fail the moment an editor changed it.

Media library test page Each section names a part of the media library, links to it on this service and lists steps to try it. The sample images are in the library already: the service puts them there with the pages under /development-testing. Sign in as the dev admin first ( sign in as the dev admin ). The service puts these pages back as they were each time it starts. Edits to the pages are lost then, but changes to the sample images stay. The library, upload and image pages Media library The sample PNG The sample photo (JPEG) The sample animation (GIF) The sample SVG Open the media library. Search for “blocks”, then use the filters “Unused” and “Missing alt text”. Drag two or more image files onto the upload area. Each file shows its progress, then a link to its image page. Open the sample PNG. Change its alt text, caption, credit and tags, then save. Check the audit log for the change. Under “Where the image is used”, check that the Image test page and the Media rich text test page are listed. Under “Replace the image”, choose another file and select “Upload new version”. The image page shows version 2, and the Image test page shows the new file. Duplicate check: save the sample PNG’s file , then upload it again. The library says the image is already there and links to it. The library uses the full width of the screen. On a wide screen the grid shows more than three images in a row. Above the images, choose “Details” in the View list. The page changes at once, and the address has view=details. Each image is a table row: a small thumbnail, the name, and its type, dimensions, file size, alt text, uses and who uploaded it, and when. Choose “Large”. Each image is on its own row, at a large size, with the same facts. Search, tick a filter, select Apply, or go to page 2. The view stays. “Clear search and filters” keeps it too. The Image widget, crop and focal point Image test page Edit the Image test page Open the Image test page. Each image comes from the library, at the width and crop the widget sets. Edit the page. Open an Image widget and select “Choose image” to open the picker. Search, choose and upload from the picker. Select “Crop image”. Try each crop shape, then drag the crop box. Type a crop to see the crop box follow it. Select “Set focal point” and click the part to keep, or use the arrow keys. Select “Crop image” and choose the 16:9 shape. “Set focal point” is now turned off, and a hint says why: the crop is already in that shape, so the focal point has no effect. Choose the Free shape, or select “Reset crop”. “Set focal point” is turned on again. Tick “This image is decorative”. The alt text clears, and the page writes an empty alt. Rich text with library images Media rich text test page Edit the Media rich text test page Open the page. Each image is a library image with signed, resized copies. Edit the page. In a rich text widget, select Insert/edit image, then the browse button, to choose from the library. Paste an image into the editor. It uploads to the library, and the editor then uses the library file. In the image dialog, tick “Image is decorative”. The image gets an empty alt and role="presentation", and the editor gives no alt text warning. Remove the alt text from an image that is not decorative. The editor shows a warning. Choose a library image in the image dialog. Select “Constrain proportions” to unlock it, then give the image another shape, for example a width of 400 and a height of 200. Save and publish. The page shows the image in that shape, also in a narrow window. The “An image stretched in the editor” section of the test page shows one. Move embedded images into the library Embedded image test page Move embedded images Open the Embedded image test page. Its image is a data: image inside the page text. Open Move embedded images. The dry run lists the page and the number of images it will move. Select the “Move … images” button. The page now shows a library image, and the library has the new image. Run the move again. It has nothing to do. To put the data: image back, restart the service, or press “Seed sample CMS pages” under System administration. A content block with an image Edit the image content block The block’s version history The sample photo’s image page Open the block’s version history. The current version shows the sample photo. Open the sample photo’s image page. Under “Used in these content blocks”, the block is listed. Edit the block and add another library image with the image dialog. Save, then check the new image’s image page. Alt text and size reports Alt text report Size report Open the alt text report. The sample animation has no alt text, and the Media rich text test page uses the photo with the weak alt text “photo”. The decorative image on the Media rich text test page is not listed. Open the size report. It shows the totals, the space the resized copies use and the largest images. Content staging export and import Content staging Export the /development-testing pages. The bundle holds mediaAssets and mediaFiles for every image the pages and blocks use. Import the same bundle. The result says “Images: … already here”. Import it on another stack. The images arrive with the same ids, and the pages show them. The bundle wins. Change the alt text of a sample image in the library, then import the bundle again. The result says “1 updated”, and the image has the bundle’s alt text again. Import never deletes an image. Use “Delete unused images” for that. Delete unused images Media library, unused images only Upload two images with the same new word in their names, for example test-unused. Open the library. Tick “Not used on any page”, search for the word, and select Apply. Select “Delete unused images”. The confirmation page lists only the unused images that match the search. Select “Delete 2 images”. The library says how many it deleted. The audit log has a “Unused images deleted from the media library” row. The sample images are used by these pages, so they are never listed. The picker needs the Media section Role settings As the dev admin, untick Media for the editor role (cypmd_content_access_user) and save. Sign in as the dev editor (open /dev/impersonate/editor) and edit the Image test page. The Image widget has no “Choose image” button, only the Image ID field. The rich text editor takes no pasted images. Type the id of a sample image into the Image ID field and save. The widget shows it. Sign in as the dev admin again, tick Media for the editor role and save. SVG sanitising Save this text as hostile.svg, then upload it to the library. The upload is accepted, and the stored file has no script, event handler, javascript: link, external address, @import or foreignObject. Open the stored file to see what is left. Save this text as entity.svg, then upload it. The library refuses it, because it has a DTD. ]> The library serves an SVG with its own content security policy. Open the developer tools, then open the sample SVG’s file and look at its Content-Security-Policy header. Signed resized copies A resized or cropped copy must carry the signature the server adds to its address. A changed or missing signature, or a width outside the fixed set, gets an error. The original file (works) A copy 640 pixels wide, with no signature (error 400) A copy with a changed signature (error 400) A width outside the fixed set (error 400) Open the Image test page and look at the page source. Each src and srcset address has w= and sig=. Open one of those addresses. Then change one letter of its sig= value. The changed address gets error 400. Open the links above. Only the original file works.
